note: Vikramashila University founded by Dharmapala — taught in s2 (NIOS Lesson 8: Dharmapala patron of Buddhism, founded Vikramashila near Bhagalpur; claims c17, c47). Practice q03 repeats it.
Tripartite struggle participants = Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas for Kanauj — core of s3 (IGNOU Unit 5; NIOS Lesson 8; claims c18, c43). Practice q04, q36 repeat it.

Rana Pratap's dynasty (Sisodiya) — primary chapter HIS-13 (medieval Mewar). This chapter's fetched sources mention only the Guhilas of Mewar among Rajput states; the Sisodiya/Rana Pratap link is not in any fetched source, so it is not taught here.
Gangaikondacholapuram founded by Rajendra I — taught in s6 (NIOS Lesson 8: Rajendra I defeated Mahipala, founded Gangaikondacholapuram, took the title 'Gangaikonda'; claim c53).

Sandhyakar Nandi, author of the Ramacharitam and court poet of the Palas — neither Sandhyakar Nandi nor the Ramacharitam appears in any source fetched for this chapter (NCERT VI, IGNOU Units 5/7, BHIC-132 Unit 4, NIOS Module 1). Source gap; not taught rather than filled from memory.
Vikramsila founded by Dharmapala — same fact as WBCS-2016-Q149, taught in s2 (claims c17, c47).

Khajuraho's name first referred to in the 11th century by Alberuni (alt HIS-10). The chapter does teach Khajuraho and the Chandella-built Kandariya Mahadeva temple (s7, NIOS; claim c60), but the Alberuni first-reference point itself appears in no fetched source — the specific tested fact is a source gap, so marked untaught.

'Balhar' (Balhara) as the Arab travellers' designation for the Rashtrakuta king — the term Balhara does not appear in any fetched source (the Rashtrakutas themselves are taught in s3/s6 via claims c38, c49, c50). Source gap; not taught.

Rajaraja I was called Arumolivarman before his coronation — Rajaraja I's reign, Brihadesvara temple and land survey are taught in s6 (claims c51, c52), but the pre-coronation name Arumolivarman appears in no fetched source. Source gap; not taught.

Chalukya king who defeated Harshavardhana = Pulakeshin II (primary chapter HIS-08; alt HIS-09). Taught in s6 and s1: NCERT VI and IGNOU BHIC-132 Unit 4 both state Pulakeshin II checked Harsha at the Narmada (claims c03, c40).
Chola king titled 'Gangaikonda' = Rajendra Chola I — taught in s6 (NIOS Lesson 8; claim c53). Same fact cluster as WBCS-2018-Q164.
Gopala, founder of the Pala dynasty — taught in s2 (IGNOU Unit 5: chiefs elected Gopala; NIOS: Gopala founder of the Pala dynasty; claims c16, c46). Practice q02 repeats it.

Kamarupa = ancient name of Assam (alt HIS-08). Kamarupa is taught in s2/s4 only as an eastern kingdom conquered by Devapala and Ramapala (IGNOU Unit 5; claims c23, c26); no fetched source equates Kamarupa with modern Assam, so the specific tested equation is a source gap — marked untaught.

Ratha temples of Mahabalipuram built by the Pallavas — taught in s6 by a stated chain: NCERT VI (fess110) places the Mahabalipuram monolithic temples on the coast ruled by the Pallavas of Tondaimandalam and NCERT VI (fess109) names the Pallavas as that coast's rulers (claims c12, c04); the chapter states this chain explicitly rather than claiming a direct 'ratha = Pallava' quote.

Jayadeva, author of the Gita Govinda, court poet of Lakshmana Sena — taught in s7 with a disclosed discrepancy: NIOS says the Gita Govinda was composed 'in Bengal under the Pala kings' (claim c58), while IGNOU states Lakshmanasena was a patron of poets (claim c28); the chapter's exam_note box tells students the exam answer is Lakshmana Sena and shows both source sentences.
Rajatarangini written by Kalhana — taught in s7 (NIOS Lessons 1 and 8; claims c57, c59). Practice q09 repeats it.
